summary_html: Court orders a **service plan or supervision** period following a substantiated finding. The goal is rehabilitation and reunification consistent with federal 'reasonable-efforts' requirements.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed a disposition order requiring a father to complete a domestic violence assessment, holding that once a child is adjudicated dependent the juvenile court has continuing jurisdiction and may impose any condition on a parent that is reasonable, proportionate, and calculated to serve the child's best interest.
key_cases.relevance: It states the Utah test — reasonableness, proportionality, and connection to the child's best interest — for every court-ordered service condition.
key_cases.quote: Under section 78A-6-117(2), the juvenile court may impose conditions on a parent so long as the conditions are "reasonable."

key_cases.holding: The Court held that Title II of the ADA applies to the provision of reunification services under Utah's child welfare statutes, but affirmed because the juvenile court acted within its discretion in finding the requested modifications to the reunification plan unreasonable.
key_cases.relevance: It establishes that a court-ordered service plan must be assessed for reasonable modifications when a parent has a disability and invokes the ADA.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the ADA applies to the provision of reunification services

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination, holding that DCFS's individualized modifications to the mother's service plan for her learning disabilities, agoraphobia, and domestic-violence history satisfied both the reasonable-efforts requirement and Title II of the ADA.
key_cases.relevance: It applies the ADA to court-ordered service plans and describes the accommodations that make reunification efforts reasonable.
key_cases.quote: Title II of the ADA prohibits public entities from discriminating against individuals with disabilities

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination of both parents' rights for serious emotional abuse, rejecting their constitutional challenges, their ineffective-assistance claims, and their attacks on the findings, and upholding the determinations that DCFS made reasonable reunification efforts and that termination was strictly necessary.
key_cases.relevance: It is a detailed recent illustration of what reasonable efforts and a court-ordered service plan look like in practice, including when therapy may properly be discontinued.
key_cases.quote: The juvenile court's determination that termination of Parents' parental rights was strictly necessary to advance the children's best interest was supported by the record

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed, holding that the juvenile court had subject matter jurisdiction because the mother voluntarily placed K.F. in state custody, that the order ending reunification and setting a goal of individualized permanency was final and appealable and appropriate where compelling reasons ruled out reunification, adoption, guardianship and kinship placement, and that the juvenile court's findings on service-plan compliance and on DCFS's reasonable efforts were owed broad discretion and were not clearly in error.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Utah Supreme Court authority on court-ordered service plans and the deference owed a juvenile court's finding that DCFS's efforts under that plan were reasonable.
key_cases.quote: appellate courts defer to juvenile courts on matters of credibility, and juvenile courts have broad discretion in determining whether reasonable reunification efforts were made

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination, holding that the juvenile court is presumed to have applied the clear-and-convincing standard absent record evidence to the contrary, that the State made out a prima facie case of reasonable efforts, and that the court did not abuse its discretion in determining after trial that DCFS had made reasonable reunification efforts.
key_cases.relevance: It is the current Utah statement of how a reasonable-efforts determination on a court-ordered service plan is reviewed, and of what a parent must show to upset one.
key_cases.quote: we discern no abuse of the juvenile court's discretion in its ultimate determination, made as factfinder after trial, that DCFS provided reasonable efforts toward reunification
